Keywords: Sokha light plough soils and draft power
RagShortTexts: A light plough’s usefulness depends on soil and draft animals.
Maintained tools and seed reserves sustain the next crop.

Variants.Content: A sokha-type light implement suits particular ground; soil, roots and draft power change the work. Households repair tools and reserve seed. More cultivated land also requires sowing, harvesting and storage labor.
Campaigning removes workers and draft power during limited seasons. An injured requisitioned animal reduces both transport and its household’s cultivated ground.
Equal labor days impose unequal losses across draft resources. Preserving seed and tools sustains future rents better than short-term extraction.
Broken tools need woodwork and iron repairs; borrowed animals create obligations. Harvest must cover seed, dues and these costs before household meals.
